ca_pinnacles_national_park.blurb: Pinnacles National Park sits on California's Central Coast, a place of rugged volcanic formations. The stone is volcanic breccia, a good deal softer and looser than the granite or basalt at many better-known destinations, so test holds and give yourself extra time. Sport routes outnumber trad, with some top-ropes, a few aid lines and a handful of boulder problems. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to a few 5.13 and 5.14 lines, concentrated between 5.9 and 5.11 with a healthy supply of moderates. Most lines are steep, bolt-protected faces, and the easier ones can be bold. The East Side holds the more solid rock, while the West Side has the longest routes on more brittle formations, where a helmet is sensible. High Peaks adds a third cluster of climbing.

wa_mount_erie.blurb: Mount Erie is the high point of Fidalgo Island near Anacortes in northwest Washington, with views toward the Olympics and Deception Pass. The rock is diorite. It is a compact, versatile place where toprope, sport, trad and multipitch climbing all turn up, with short walks to most cliffs. Sport routes make up roughly half the climbing and trad about a third, plus some top-ropes and a modest boulder scene. Grades centre on 5.8 to 5.10, with 5.9 and 5.10 the most common, a fair number of easier lines, and a few 5.11s and 5.12s. The crags face south, and the rain shadow of the Olympics can leave conditions drier than nearby areas. Big sub-areas include Powerline, Orange Area, Skyline Arete and the Main Wall.

vt_smugglers_notch_bouldering.blurb: Smugglers' Notch Bouldering lies in northern Vermont, at roughly 2,100 feet, with problems strewn along both sides of the road. The boulders are said to draw more climbers than the cliffs and even the ice nearby. Nearly everything here is a boulder problem, and the spread is wide: a big base of V0 to V4, a solid middle of V5 to V8, and a thinner tail that runs well into the double digits. The two biggest clusters are the Top of the Notch Boulders and the boulders behind the main parking lot by the visitor center, with smaller groups around Roots and Bingham Falls. Expect a walk of a mile or two to reach many of them. Crowds can swing from nobody to busy.

nc_crowders_mountain.blurb: Crowders Mountain is a state park in the North Carolina Piedmont, a wooded mountain setting handy to a major city, which means nice weekends can feel crowded. Bouldering is over half of the climbing, centred on the Dixon School Boulders, where the stone is a metamorphosed quartz-pebble conglomerate and holds come from weathering seams and edges. Problems run mostly V0 to V4, with a tail up to V8 and a few harder. Roped climbing sits on the main crags and spires, mostly trad with some bolted leads and top-rope setups, and Hidden Wall is a smaller sport crag. Grades spread from easy fifth class up to around 5.12, with the most routes at 5.8 and 5.10. Slips near the tops of cliffs are common.

wv_summersville_gauley_river_area.blurb: Summersville Lake and the Gauley River form one of the New River Gorge region's sport climbing centres, on Nuttall sandstone around the reservoir. Sport dominates by a wide margin, with a modest amount of trad and a few boulders. Routes are short, roughly 30 to 100 feet, and range from near vertical to severely overhanging, with pockets, huecos, slopers and jugs. Grades cluster hard: the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with a few 5.13s and 5.14s and only a small supply of easier lines. Lake level shapes the season, since high summer water covers some lines and suits swimming, while cooler months reveal more crags. Much of the rock faces south, which helps in cold weather. The biggest sectors are the main lake area, Long Point and Whippoorwill.

ca_wonderland_north.blurb: Wonderland North is the northern part of the Wonderland of Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,200 feet. It is a quiet, remote corner that offers a break from the crowds of busier Joshua Tree venues. The ground is flat, but walks in run an hour or more, and the farthest crags take up to an hour and a half. Trad dominates by a wide margin, with a smaller group of sport routes and some top-ropes. Grades are mostly 5.7 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, plus a few 5.12 and 5.13 lines. The larger sub-areas are the North Wonderland Approach, the Middle Kingdom, Grey Giant Area and Willow Hole Area.
